text.tspan: Department of Chemistry, Graduate School of Science, Kyoto University, Japan
Approximate Functionals for Multistate Density Functional Theory
[1] Lu, Y.; Gao, J. Multistate Density Functional Theory of Excited States. J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2022, 13, 7762–7769
[2] Theophilou, A. K. The energy density functional formalism for excited states. J. Phys. C: Solid State Physics 1979, 12, 5419.
An approximate L(S)DA-like matrix functional can reproduce the off-diagonal elements of the
electron-repulsion operator accurately when evaluated on the exact matrix density.
Diagonal elements of the kinetic energy, however, have large errors.
Future work: Implement variational minimization of subspace energy as a function of D(r).
Recently Lu and Gao formulated a rigorous multistate density functional theory, where
ground and excited states are treated on the same footing [1].
What is still missing are approximations to the universal kinetic and exchange-correlation
matrix functionals. Here an approximate LDA-like functional is explored.
Test Case: Dissociation Curve of LiF
•Plug D(r) into matrix functionals for electron-electron repulsion, kinetic energy
Lu and Gao's Matrix Density Functional Theory
•The fundamental variable is the matrix density D(r), the projection of the density
operator into the subspace of the lowest N states
Subspace 𝕍 N is found by minimizing
Eigenvalue of N x N matrix H[D*(r)]
Properties of the Universal Matrix Functional F[D(r)]
Under a basis transformation L in the subspace 𝕍N, wavefunctions, projections of the density
⇝ F[D] is an analytical matrix functional
⇝ F[D] has no explicit dependence on number of states N (=dim D(r))
For N=1 the F[D] reduces to the universal ground state functional F[𝛒].
Recipe for "translating" ground state F[𝛒] to multistate F[D] ⇒ reuse same Taylor coefficients
• Self-Interaction Correction (SIC) for core-orbitals ρα1s is a constant, geometry-independent
Approximate Matrix Functional of Electron-Electron Repulsion
